prerequisites: Ciencia y tecnología de los materiales/V12G380V01301 (Science and Technology of Materials)

learning_outcomes.text: Knows the main material forming and transformation processes used in industry.
Demonstrates ability to select the most appropriate manufacturing process for obtaining basic parts from a given material.
Knows the main material joining processes used in industry.
Understands the complex interrelationships between material properties and forming and joining processes to optimize properties and productivity across a wide range of industrial sectors.
Knows the characteristics of materials most commonly used in Engineering.
Knows the evolution of different types of materials and their potential forming processes.
Knows and applies criteria for selecting the most suitable material for a specific application.
Analyzes and proposes operational solutions to problems in the field of materials engineering.
Interprets, analyzes, synthesizes and draws conclusions and results from measurements and tests.
Writes texts with the appropriate structure for communication objectives. Presents the text to an audience using appropriate strategies and means.
Identifies own information needs and uses available resources, spaces, and services to design and execute searches appropriate to the thematic area.
Carries out assigned tasks based on basic guidelines given by the professor, deciding on the duration of parts, including personal contributions, and expanding information sources.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Materials Engineering. Thematic Unit I: In-service behavior.
Presentation of the course. Evaluation criteria. Tutorials.

Topic 1. Fatigue: Concept and importance. Characteristics of fracture surfaces. S-N curve. Palmgren-Miner damage accumulation criterion. Effect of mean stress: Gerber and Goodman criteria. Factors affecting fatigue life.

Topic 2. Fracture Mechanics: Structural integrity and its relation to the presence of defects. Griffith and Irwin theories. Fracture criteria in linear elastic media. Stress analysis around cracks: plane stress and plane strain conditions. Fracture toughness in plane strain. Application of fracture mechanics to crack growth under cyclic loads. Prediction of service life.

Topic 3. Creep: Effect of temperature on mechanical strength. Creep curve. Design parameters. Creep tests for metals and polymers. Dependence of creep on stress and temperature. Data extrapolation. Development of creep-resistant alloys. Material selection. Deformation mechanisms.

Topic 4. Fundamentals and technology of corrosion: Socio-economic importance. Classification of different corrosion processes. Electrochemical corrosion. Thermodynamic aspects. Electrode potential and Pourbaix diagrams. Kinetic aspects. Corrosion rate. Polarization phenomena. Passivation. Corrosion control methods: design strategies, material and/or medium modification, protection by coatings, electrochemical protection (catodic and anodic).
Thematic Unit II: Metal forming, treatment, and joining techniques.

Topic 5: Casting: advanced molding processes: Technological characteristics of casting: compactness, castability and crackability. Alloys for molding. Directional molding, single crystal molding and amorphous metals. Liquid metal forging (Squeeze Casting). Casting and processing of semi-solid alloys (Thixocasting and thixoforging).

Topic 6: Response of materials to cold and hot plastic deformation forming: Strain hardening. Factors influencing plastic deformation. Elimination of work hardening: recrystallization annealing. Hot working: dynamic restoration and recrystallization. Structures obtained by casting: effect of cooling rate and alloying elements. Cold and hot forming.

Topic 7. Heat and thermomechanical treatments: Quenching and hardenability. Tempering. Stepped quenching (martempering). Isothermal bainitic transformation (austempering). Thermomechanical treatments: concept and classification. High and low temperature thermomechanical treatments (controlled rolling and ausforming), with plastic deformation during transformation (isoforming) and subsequent to austenite transformation (marforming and perlitoforming).

Topic 8. Welding metallurgy: Classification of processes according to AWS. Thermal cycle: influencing factors. Welded joint zones. Solidification of the weld pool: epitaxy and competitive growth. As-cast structure. Multi-pass welding. Heat Affected Zone (HAZ). Solid solution strengthened materials. Overheating zone. Work hardened materials: recrystallization and grain growth. Transformation hardened materials. Precipitation hardened materials. Post-weld heat treatments.
Thematic Unit IV: Structural materials.

Topic 9. Structural and stainless steels: Hot-rolled general purpose steels. Microalloyed steels. Steels with improved atmospheric corrosion resistance. Steels for quenching and tempering. Steels for low temperatures. Stainless steels. Characteristics of the passive film. Classification.
Topic 10. Aluminum alloys: Strengthening of aluminum. General classification of aluminum alloys. Aluminum alloys for forging. Aluminum alloys for casting.
PRACTICE PROGRAM

Practice 1. Fractography and fatigue behavior: Macroscopic and microscopic characteristics of fracture surfaces. Scanning electron microscopy. Case studies. Fatigue: fundamentals of the test. Obtaining the Wöhler curve. Analysis of factors influencing fatigue strength. Problem solving.

Practice 2. Corrosion technology. Anticorrosive protection: Electrochemical techniques for the study of corrosion phenomena. Metallographic study. Coating evaluation techniques. Thickness and adhesion determination. Evaluation of different failure mechanisms.
Practice 3: Metallographic study: effect of forming on material structure: Structures obtained by casting: effect of cooling rate and alloying elements. Cold forming and hot forming.
Practice 4: Metallography of heat-treated alloys: Heat treatment of steels. Heat treatment of light alloys.
Practice 5: Hardenability evaluation. Jominy test: Obtaining the Jominy curve. Principle, objective and field of application. Test methodology and expression of results.
Practice 6. Inspection by liquid penetrants and magnetic particles: Principle, objective and field of application. Test methodology and inspection report.

Practice 7. Industrial radiography and ultrasonics (part I): Industrial radiography. Principle, objective and field of application. Test methodology. Ultrasound generation. Emission-reception and pulse-echo methods. Ultrasonic inspection: calibration, thickness determination by multiple echo technique.

Practice 8. Ultrasonic inspection (part II): Examination and verification of metal parts with normal probe. In-situ concrete structure evaluation. Sclerometer: determination of surface hardness and relation to concrete compressive strength. Inspection by direct transmission. Determination of propagation velocity in indirect transmission. Correlation between ultrasonic pulse velocity and strength.
Practice 9. Tutored work presentation: Each student will participate in the presentation of their group's work and answer questions posed by both the teacher and classmates from other groups.
teaching_methods: Laboratory practices: Activities applying knowledge to specific situations and acquiring basic and procedural skills related to the subject matter. Developed in laboratories with specialized equipment.

Tutored work: Each work group will prepare a document on the subject matter following the elaboration guide available on the e-learning platform. The guidelines regarding general structure and length must be respected. Group members must conduct extensive bibliographic research consulting various information sources. After completing the report, each student will participate in the presentation of their group's work and answer questions posed by both the teacher and other students, opening a debate related to the proposed topic.
Seminar: Intends to monitor student work and resolve difficulties in understanding course content.

Problem solving: Activity where the professor provides students with a series of problems and/or exercises related to the subject, for them to work on at home. Students must develop appropriate or correct solutions by performing routines, applying formulas or algorithms, applying information transformation procedures, and interpreting results. Problem solving will be done in class, by the professor or a student.
Lectures: Oral and direct exposition by the professor of fundamental knowledge corresponding to the course topics.

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practices (includes reports, attendance, participation, and practical sessions exam)
Tutored work (includes memory quality, group work, and presentation/communication skills)
Partial Exam I (theoretical content: short questions, problems, multiple choice)
Partial Exam II (theoretical content: short questions, problems, multiple choice, global understanding)

assessment_rules: For the 1st evaluation period, a minimum of 40% must be achieved in each theoretical exam (Partial Exam I and Partial Exam II), or alternatively, a global minimum of 50% (3.5 points out of 7) across both partials. If these minimums are not met, the course is considered failed, and the maximum grade recorded will be 4.5 points, regardless of the sum of other sections. If the minimums in the exams are met, the grades from tutored work and practices will be added, requiring a minimum of 5 points out of 10 to pass. Students for the 2nd evaluation period (July exam) will take a single written exam covering all theoretical content (70% of the grade), while retaining the grades from practices and tutored work (30%), with the same minimum requirements as the 1st edition. For global evaluation, students will take a single written exam covering all course content (theoretical and practical) on the official date, needing a minimum of 5 points out of 10 to pass. In the September extraordinary call, only the global evaluation system will be used.
